stories.title: Things to Do with Kids in Colorado Springs This Weekend (October 16–18)
stories.angle: Weekend Family Roundup — Required Thursday slot

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: This weekend in COS: Pumpkinfest (Fri–Sun, $8), Boo at the Zoo (Fri, 4pm, tickets required), free Robotics Workshop (Sat, 11am, ages 5–14), and Barks & Boos Fall Fest (Sun, FREE). Full list ↓ #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM MT

It's a packed fall weekend in Colorado Springs, and we've got your full rundown.

Pumpkinfest at Venetucci Farm is open Friday through Sunday. Admission is $8 per person, kids 3 and under are free, and Friday hours run 9:30 AM to 2 PM. It's one of the most beloved fall traditions in COS — bring layers and expect muddy boots. 🎃

Boo at the Zoo officially opened last night, with dates every weekend through Halloween. Hours are 4–8:30 PM. This one sells out — advance tickets only at cmzoo.org (members still need a ticket, but get $5 off). No walk-ups allowed.

Free Robotics Workshop at the DoubleTree by Hilton Colorado Springs: Saturday, October 17 at 11 AM. Kids ages 5–14, no charge. It's a great rainy-day option if the weather doesn't cooperate.

Barks & Boos Fall Fest is Sunday, October 18, 11 AM–3 PM, and it's completely free. There's a pup costume parade — yes, dogs are invited 🐾 — and plenty of fall festival activities for the whole family.

The Cool Science Festival also runs through Sunday the 18th if your crew leans toward the science end of the spectrum.

Which one's on your weekend list?
facebook.image_caption:
Window: 11:00 AM MT

Pumpkin patches, robotics workshops, and a dog costume parade — COS has a full fall weekend lined up. Which one is your family hitting? 🎃🐾

stories.title: Today Was Game Day. Coronado Didn't Show — and the Forfeit Controversy Keeps Growing.
stories.angle: Oct 15 game day update — two COS forfeits confirmed, Palmer Ridge split

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: Today was the day. Coronado was scheduled to play Lutheran High — but didn't show. That's two COS school forfeits over racism allegations. Palmer Ridge says it WILL play. CHSAA investigation continues. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:00 AM MT

Today was supposed to be game day.

Coronado High School was scheduled to play Lutheran High in Parker on Thursday, October 15. Coronado didn't show up — District 11 announced the forfeit on October 12 after asking both Lutheran and CHSAA for an unequivocal public statement denouncing racism. Neither organization provided one.

It's now the second forfeit involving a Colorado Springs-area school. Air Academy forfeited its homecoming game against Lutheran earlier in October. Both forfeits stem from allegations that students associated with Lutheran made racist remarks toward cheerleaders from multiple COS schools — including Sand Creek, Rampart, and Colorado Springs High School — during games this fall.

Lutheran High has said the students accused of racist behavior were not enrolled at their school and that its own investigation is ongoing. CHSAA says it wasn't notified of the Coronado forfeit through proper channels; it learned through D11's public statement.

Under CHSAA rules, Lutheran receives two automatic wins.

Palmer Ridge is breaking ranks — the school has said it will still play Lutheran on October 30.

The NAACP has requested a meeting with Lutheran's administration. State Rep. Regina English has also weighed in. The CHSAA investigation continues.

How are you feeling about how your school district has handled this?

Window: 1:00 PM MT

Today was the scheduled Coronado–Lutheran game day. Coronado didn't show. That's two forfeits from COS-area schools now — and the conversation in our community is only growing. 🏈

stories.title: D11's $775 Million Bond: What Colorado Springs Homeowners Would Pay If It Passes
stories.angle: Property tax impact details — KKTV Oct 15 reporting

x_posts.label: Post 3-1
x_posts.text: D11's $775M bond: if it passes, the average COS homeowner pays about $264 more per year in property taxes. Covers HVAC, safety upgrades, asbestos removal, and classroom modernization. Vote Nov. 3. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Window: 12:00 PM MT

D11's $775 million bond measure is on the November 3 ballot — and KKTV crunched the numbers this week on what it would actually cost you.

The average Colorado Springs homeowner would pay about $264 more per year in property taxes if Issue 4A passes. That works out to roughly $22 a month.

What does the bond fund?

- Safety and security upgrades at aging school buildings
- HVAC replacement and asbestos removal
- Career and Technical Education program improvements
- Updated classrooms and libraries

The D11 school board voted 6–1 in August to put this on the ballot. El Paso County drop boxes are already open if you're voting early, and the election closes November 3.

You can find the full breakdown at d11.org/4A.

stories.title: ONTHEWEI Baby Bath Seats Recalled and Dresser Warning Issued: What Parents Need to Know
stories.angle: Two CPSC actions this week — bath seat recall + dresser tip-over warning

x_posts.label: Post 4-1
x_posts.text: RECALL ALERT: 2,140 ONTHEWEI baby bath seats recalled due to tip-over risk. Seats can tip over during use — stop using immediately. Request a full refund at cpsc.gov/Recalls. Ages affected: infants. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Window: 3:00 PM MT

Two product safety notices families with young children need to know about this week.

ONTHEWEI Baby Bath Seats (recalled): About 2,140 units have been recalled by the CPSC because the seats are unstable and can tip over during use, violating the mandatory infant bath seat standard. If you own one, stop using it immediately. No injuries have been reported, but a tipping bath seat during infant bathing is a drowning risk. Contact the company for a full refund — and find details at cpsc.gov/Recalls.

Jocoevol 6-Drawer Dressers (warning): The CPSC has warned consumers to stop using these dressers because they violate the mandatory clothing storage unit standard for tip-over and entrapment risks. Dresser tip-overs are one of the leading causes of furniture-related fatalities in young children. If you have one in a child's bedroom, anchor it to the wall now or stop using it.

Neither recall required a major purchase — a bath seat or a dresser — but the hazards are serious for the smallest kids in your home.

Do you have any of these products at home? 👀

stories.title: The AAP Says Kids Should Get Their Flu Shot by End of October. Here's What Parents Need to Know.
stories.angle: End-of-October AAP deadline — two-dose rule for first-timers

x_posts.label: Post 5-1
x_posts.text: AAP reminder: all kids 6 months and older should get their flu shot by end of October. Don't wait — peak flu season is coming. Talk to your pediatrician this week about the 2026–27 vaccine. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Window: 5:00 PM MT

October is almost halfway over — and the American Academy of Pediatrics says the clock is ticking on flu shots for kids.

The AAP's 2026–27 influenza guidelines recommend that all children 6 months and older (without medical contraindications) receive their annual flu vaccine, and the ideal window to get it done is by the end of October.

Here's the thing parents of younger kids especially need to know: if your child is getting the flu vaccine for the very first time, they need two doses, four weeks apart. That means if you haven't started yet, you're already tight on timing before peak flu season kicks in.

Your pediatrician's office, most pharmacies, and many school-based health programs in COS offer the vaccine. Kids under 8 who need both doses can often get the second one booked at the same appointment.

Have your kids gotten their flu shot yet this season? 💉

Window: 7:00 PM MT

End-of-October deadline for kids' flu shots — that's the AAP's guidance for the 2026–27 season. All children 6 months+ should be vaccinated. If yours haven't gotten theirs yet, this week is a great time to call the pediatrician.
